tour.1: These four figures are NCRB counts for {last}. Hover over or tap the underlined words under a figure to see exactly what it counts.
tour.6: Every number on the site can be downloaded in Excel or CSV, with the NCRB table it came from and the section of law it falls under.
tip.cs: The share of cases police finished investigating in which they filed a charge-sheet, the formal accusation that sends a case to court.
tip.inv: Cases the police were still investigating on 31 December of that year.
tip.court: Cases sent for trial that year plus every case still waiting from earlier years.
tip.trials: Trials that ended that year in a conviction, an acquittal or a discharge.
tip.cr: Convictions as a share of the trials that ended that year. This is the measure NCRB itself uses.
tip.pend: Cases still waiting for a verdict on 31 December, including cases that reached court in earlier years.
tip.cp: Cases still pending at the end of the year as a share of all cases before the courts that year.
tip.rate: Cases recorded for every lakh (1,00,000) women, using the female population NCRB projects for that year.
tip.ipc: The Indian Penal Code (IPC) applied to offences before 1 July 2024. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced it from that date.
tip.pocso: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Most sexual offences against girls under 18 are booked under this law.
pr.delhi: In {last} police in Delhi recorded {rape} rape cases and {pocso} cases of penetrative sexual assault of girls under POCSO. That is {rate} rapes for every lakh women in Delhi, against {india} for India.
pr.bihar: Police in Bihar recorded {rape} rape cases and {pocso} POCSO cases of penetrative sexual assault in {last}, or {rate} rapes for every lakh women. A low recorded rate can come from less crime or from less recording, and NCRB's figures cannot tell the two apart.
pr.india: Across India, {pend} of every 100 rape cases before the courts in {last} were still waiting for a verdict at the end of the year, and {conv} of every 100 rape trials that ended that year ended in a conviction.
home.courts.t: {conv} in 100 rape trials that ended in {y} ended in a conviction
pr.chart: Rape cases recorded for every lakh women in Delhi, Bihar and India, {y0} to {y1}. A higher line can mean more crime or more recording, and the figures cannot tell the two apart.

crime.intro: Police in India recorded {b} cases under this heading in {y1}, against {a} in {y0}. That is {r} for every lakh women.

tourp.2: The Protests page sets out the cases and protests of September 2026, each with the outlet that reported it, and what the records say about Delhi, Bihar and India.
tourp.3: The Police and courts page follows each crime from the FIR to the verdict. A flow chart shows where the cases went, and a field of stitches shows every case before the courts in a year.
tourp.5: The States page has a map for each crime and year. Every state and union territory has a page of its own with every year from 2017 to {last}.
tourp.4: The Crimes page has a chart for each of seventeen crimes, year by year, and each crime has a page that shows every state.
trend.pair: Rape and penetrative sexual assault of girls under POCSO are recorded separately, so the two are shown together.
cx.nfhs.lead: In NFHS-5, {pos} in every 100 ever-married women aged 18 to 49 said a husband had been physically or sexually violent towards them. Of all women who had faced physical or sexual violence from anyone, {never} in 100 had never sought help and never told anyone, and {sought} in 100 had sought help.
cx.nfhs.cap: Women aged 18 to 49 who had faced physical or sexual violence, by what they did about it. NFHS-5, India.
cx.nfhs.never: Never sought help or told anyone
cx.nfhs.told: Told someone but did not seek help
cx.nfhs.c1: Violence by a husband, physical or sexual
cx.nfhs.c3: Never sought help or told anyone
cx.ncw.lead: The Commission received {n} complaints in {y}, {up} in 100 of them from Uttar Pradesh. {dv} were about domestic violence and {rape} about rape or attempted rape.
cx.ncw.cap: Complaints received by the National Commission for Women each year, India.
cx.adsi.lead: Police recorded {f} suicides of women in {y}. {hw} of them, or {share} in every 100, were housewives.
cx.adsi.cap: Suicides of women recorded by police each year, India.
cx.bprd.lead: On 1 January 2024 India had {n} women police, {pct} in every 100 officers, up from {old} in 100 four years earlier. There were {ps} women police stations.
cx.bprd.cap: Women and men in the police, actual strength, 1 January 2024.
cx.ftsc.lead: On 30 April 2026, {courts} fast track special courts were working, {epocso} of them for POCSO cases only, and {pend} cases were waiting in them. They decided {disp} cases in 2025. At that pace the cases waiting would take {years} years to clear, with no new case added.
cx.ftsc.cap: Cases decided by fast track special courts each year, and the cases waiting on 30 April 2026.
cx.njdg.lead: On 9 October 2026, {wf} of the {all} cases pending in district and taluka courts had been filed by a woman, {share} in every 100. {crim} of them were criminal cases.
cx.njdg.cap: Cases pending in district and taluka courts, by whether a woman filed them, 9 October 2026.
cx.nir.lead: By the end of 2025-26 the government had allocated Rs {alloc} crore to the Nirbhaya Fund and released or used Rs {rel} crore, {share} in every 100 rupees. Rs {left} crore of the allocation had not been released.
cx.nir.cap: The Nirbhaya Fund since 2013, released or used against the amount allocated, India.
cx.nir.c1: Released and used since 2013, Rs crore
cx.nir.c2: Released and used in 2025-26, Rs crore
cx.adr.lead: In August 2024, {n} sitting members of Parliament and state assemblies had declared cases of crimes against women, {mp} MPs and {mla} MLAs. {rape} of them had declared cases of rape. In March 2025 the count for MLAs alone was {n25}, {r25} of them with cases of rape.
cx.adr.cap: Sitting MPs and MLAs with declared cases of crimes against women, by state, August 2024.
iso.cap: Each figure is 1 in every 100 cases of {crime} before the courts in {y}. {conv} of them ended in a conviction that year, and {pend}, or {share} in every 100, were still waiting for a verdict when the year ended.
iso.per: Each figure is 1 in every 100 cases. A group smaller than half of 1 in 100 has no figure of its own.

ex.intro: Every figure on this site is in the table below, {n} rows from NCRB's Crime in India. Choose a crime, a place, a measure and years, search for a word, sort by any column, and download exactly the rows in view. The view is kept in the page's address, so a copied link opens the same table.
state.iso.cap: {n} cases of crimes against women were before the courts in {s} in {y}. Each figure is 1 in every 100 of them. {conv} ended in a conviction that year, and {pend}, or {share} in every 100, were still waiting for a verdict when the year ended.
state.mix.cap: All {n} crimes against women recorded in {s} in {y}, by heading. Each box is that heading's share of the state's total.
state.pocso: {share}% of the {n} cases recorded in {s} in {y} were booked under the POCSO Act, against {ri}% across India. Rape of girls under 18 is mostly booked under POCSO and counted separately, so read the rape box and the POCSO box together.
trend.long: Before 2017 the line shows India only, and only in years when NCRB counted this heading the same way. A gap is a year when it did not.
ct.mr.p: Since 2017 NCRB's chapter on crimes against women has carried a separate heading for murder with rape or gang rape, so a rape that ends in murder is counted in that chapter under that heading. In {y} NCRB recorded {mr} such cases, beside {rape} cases of rape and {pocso} cases of rape of girls under the POCSO Act.
ct.un.p1: Police can count only the cases reported to them. In the National Family Health Survey of 2019-21 (NFHS-5), among women aged 18 to 49 who had ever experienced physical or sexual violence, {never} in every 100 had never told anyone about it, and {sought} in every 100 had sought help from anyone, the police included.
pt.vi.p1: In the National Family Health Survey of 2019-21 (NFHS-5), {pos} in every 100 ever-married women aged 18 to 49 said a husband had been physically or sexually violent towards them, and {sv} in every 100 women aged 18 to 49 said someone had been sexually violent towards them at some time in their lives. The survey asks only about the current or most recent husband, so the first figure leaves out earlier marriages.
pt.to.p1: Among the women who had experienced physical or sexual violence, {never} in every 100 had never told anyone about it, and {sought} in every 100 had sought help from anyone at all (NFHS-5).
pt.in.p1: In {y} the police had {inv} cases of crimes against women to investigate, {carry} of them left from earlier years. They filed charge-sheets in {cs}, closed {fal} as false and {ins} as true but with insufficient evidence, untraced or with no clue, and {pinv} were still under investigation when the year ended. NCRB's charge-sheeting rate, charge-sheets as a share of the cases the police finished with in the year, was {csr}%.
pt.tr.p1: In {y} the courts had {ct} cases of crimes against women before them, most of them from earlier years. Trials were completed in {tc}. Of these, {conv} ended in conviction, {acq} in acquittal and {dis} in discharge. {ptr} cases, {cp}% of the total, were still waiting for a verdict when the year ended. NCRB's conviction rate, convictions as a share of completed trials, was {cr}%.
known.p.RAPE: In {y} NCRB recorded {total} rape cases. In {known} of them ({share}%) the woman or girl knew the man accused. He was a family member in {fam} cases, a friend, online friend, live-in partner, man who had promised to marry her or separated husband in {part}, and a family friend, neighbour, employer or other man she knew in {acq}. In {unk} cases the offender was unknown or not identified.
known.p.POCSO_RAPE: In {y} NCRB recorded {total} cases of penetrative sexual assault on children under sections 4 and 6 of the POCSO Act, against girls and boys. In {known} of them ({share}%) the child knew the offender. The offender was a family member in {fam} cases, a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person in {acq}, and a friend, online friend, live-in partner or someone who had promised marriage in {part}. In {unk} cases the offender was unknown or not identified.
known.k.acq: Family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person
known.cap.RAPE: Rape cases in India by who the offender was, {y0} to {y1}, as a share of each year's cases. NCRB Crime in India, table 3A.4.
known.cap.POCSO_RAPE: POCSO cases under sections 4 and 6 in India by who the offender was, {y0} to {y1}, as a share of each year's cases. The table counts child victims of both sexes, so its total is higher than the POCSO figure for girls on this page. NCRB Crime in India, table 4A.10.
known.states: Each state's figures for {y}. States are listed in alphabetical order. Select a column heading to sort by it.
sec.p: NCRB also counts rape cases by the section of law they were registered under. In {y}, of {all} rape cases, {gang} were registered as gang rape, {rel} as rape by a relative, guardian, teacher or person in a position of trust, and {off} as rape by a police officer, public servant, member of the armed forces, or staff of a jail, remand home or hospital. {death} cases were of rape that caused the victim's death or left her in a persistent vegetative state.
sec.r.rel: By a relative, guardian, teacher or person in a position of trust
sec.r.off: By a police officer, public servant, member of the armed forces, or jail, remand home or hospital staff
sec.r.death: Causing death or a persistent vegetative state
per.p: In {y} the police arrested {arr} people for {crime}, {f} of them women, and charge-sheeted {cs}. The courts convicted {conv} people, acquitted {acq} and discharged {dis}. Most people tried in a year were arrested in earlier years, so these numbers do not follow one group of people from arrest to verdict.
per.women: The law defines rape as an offence committed by a man (IPC section 375, BNS section 63). NCRB counts everyone arrested in the cases filed under a crime heading, so these women were arrested in rape cases. The Supreme Court held in Priya Patel v State of Madhya Pradesh (12 July 2006) that a woman cannot be prosecuted for gang rape, and left open whether she can be charged with abetting it. NCRB does not say what the women were charged with.
per.none: NCRB counts the people arrested and tried, by crime, from 2020. There are no figures for {y}.
per.cap: People arrested, charge-sheeted, convicted, acquitted and discharged for {crime} in India in {y}. NCRB Crime in India, table 3A.9.
per.states: People arrested and tried for all crimes against women in each state in {y}, from NCRB table 3A.10. NCRB does not publish these figures by state for each crime. In many states more people were charge-sheeted than arrested, because the police may file a charge-sheet against a person they have not arrested. The Supreme Court held in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh (16 August 2021) that the law "does not impose an obligation on the Officer-in-charge to arrest each and every accused at the time of filing of the chargesheet". States are listed in alphabetical order. Select a column heading to sort by it.
city.p: In {y} the police in India's 19 largest cities recorded {n} cases of crimes against women, {share}% of the {all} recorded in India. The table gives each city's cases from {y0} to {y}, the share of cases the police charge-sheeted in {y}, and NCRB's rate. Cities are listed in alphabetical order. Select a column heading to sort by it.
caste.h: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women and girls
caste.p: In {y} the police recorded {sc} rape cases in which the woman or girl belonged to a Scheduled Caste ({scw} women and {scc} girls under 18) and {st} in which she belonged to a Scheduled Tribe ({stw} women and {stc} girls). The courts convicted in {csc}% of the trials they completed in Scheduled Caste cases and in {cst}% in Scheduled Tribe cases, against {call}% for all rape cases. At the end of {y}, {psc} Scheduled Caste cases and {pst} Scheduled Tribe cases were still waiting for trial.
caste.cap: Conviction rate in rape cases, {y0} to {y1}, where the woman or girl belonged to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, and for all rape cases. The conviction rate is convictions as a share of the trials completed in the year. NCRB Crime in India, Volume 2, tables 7A.5 and 7C.5, and Volume 1, table 3A.7.
caste.r.pdsc: Cases for trial still pending at year end, Scheduled Caste
caste.r.pdst: Cases for trial still pending at year end, Scheduled Tribe
caste.r.pdall: Cases for trial still pending at year end, all rape cases
caste.states: Rape cases recorded in each state in {y} in which the woman or girl belonged to a Scheduled Caste or a Scheduled Tribe, from NCRB tables 7A.2 and 7C.2. These are counts of cases. The states have very different Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe populations, so the counts cannot be compared between states. States are listed in alphabetical order. Select a column heading to sort by it.
caste.note: NCRB records these cases in Volume 2 of Crime in India, as rape booked under the IPC or BNS read with the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. Its tables list rape of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe women and girls only under that heading, so a case in which the police did not apply the Act does not appear here. The figures start in 2021 because this site does not hold the 2020 Volume 2. In 2024, table 7A.2 prints Chhattisgarh's IPC cases as 100 beside 32 BNS cases and a total of 119, so the IPC figure cannot be right. This page uses the total, which adds up.
